_meta.status: DRAFT — owner reviews the color board by eye and overrules; nothing here is ratified
_meta.law: flora_commission_template.md §3 palette_family + §8.4 RATIFIED contrast law: ONE palette family per biome, ladder slots separated by VALUE not hue, at most ONE accent species (zero allowed)
_meta.family_order: dark → light; adjacent flora-ladder slots take adjacent value steps
_meta.derivations: family hexes are a judgment pass over the sheet's own §9 prose, calibrated against sampled existing plant art where the biome has any; 'INVENTED' marks an anchor with neither prose nor art behind it
_meta.art_sampling: dominant colors sampled (PIL, backdrop-masked) from design/Jawa/worldbuilding/review/plant_art/*.detail.png per the biome rosters

derivedFrom: §9: “silver-green fuzz banding to grey fog-country darkward and waxy gold sunward”
§9: “venomvine as near-black islands” (family dark end)
arid_shrubland.note: Silver-green family; venomvine sits at the near-black end of the same ramp.

derivedFrom: §9: “hot low sun on lit faces — amber, ochre, rust — against long cool blue shadows”
§9: “The only greens are the pale ultracactus flush with the ground and the dew-line halo”
banned: saturated green anywhere but the two named greens
desert.note: Cool blue shadow is the light regime, not a flora hue.

derivedFrom: §9: “ochre, bone, rust-tan and pale gold in the sand”
§9: “a hard green line arrives with no warning … the most saturated thing on the dayside”
banned: blue sky tones (sky is bleached white)
dune_sea.note: Only strong contrast is shadow black; the green line lands like a shout.

deep_desert.accentLabel: none — zero accents claimed (§8.4 allows zero)
derivedFrom: §9: “bleached bone, pale dust, wind-glazed dark stone, salt-white. No green anywhere in the open”
§9: “no black char, because nothing has ever burned here”
deep_desert.note: Accent deliberately NONE (§8.4 allows zero); pale-and-powdery is the whole statement.

derivedFrom: §9: “bleached bone-white hardpan … punctuated by hard black shade and the scorched, oxidised colour of fresh re-entry”
§9: “a status lamp still green in the black under a hull”
banned: orange rust (rust “has not had time to go orange yet”)
fall_line.note: Flora lives in wreck shade — the family is char/heat-blued greys, not the white flats.

derivedFrom: §9: “obsidian black, glow-blue, lamp-yellow, hydrocarbon-frost grey on the rime faces”
§9: “blue darklight gammas against yellow giant flora, a harbor-at-night palette”
forsaken_crags.note: Two-tone biolum forced through §8.4: lamp-yellow IS the family's light end, glow-blue is the one accent. Owner may prefer the inverse.

derivedFrom: §9: “white dirty ice over blue-black rock … aurora green and violet as the ambient · starlight grey”
§9: “in the pans and nowhere else, the shockingly clean saturated chemistry colour”
banned: warm light of any kind (“No warm light anywhere except what the player brings”)

derivedFrom: §9: “wet black and slate ground · bone-pale trunks streaked with grey metal tears”
§9: “crystal in bruised blue and sulfur yellow; the dark red-purple films of the defeated phototrophs”
poison_forest.note: Three accent candidates in prose (sulfur yellow, bruised blue, red-purple film); sulfur drafted — needs the owner's eye.

derivedFrom: §9: “salt white and pale grey ground, dominant and everywhere · black-green and near-black in the few standing plants”
§9: “low warm amber on every starward face, because grazing light is reddened light”
banned: blue water (“the water … is never blue”)
terminator_sea.note: Family runs black-green plant → salt-white ground; the “one saturated accent per animal” rule is fauna's, not flora's.

derivedFrom: §9: “scattering-blue at distance, glass-clear and grey underfoot; transparent flora refracting”
§9: “the Burners' halos of blue fire the only warm light for a hundred kilometers”
banned: warm hues except rust/char on the fallen
the_blue_desert.note: Transparent flora: the family is what refraction TINTS, not body color — hard to anchor in flat hex; expect an overrule.

derivedFrom: §9: “red water, red fog, pink-and-blue aberrations, the grey-white of husks and sterilized matter at the burn line”
§9: “cracked clay grey-white, red-brown flood stain on the walls, moss green in the slots”
§9: “the green only ever in the blue shade”
§9: “living-wood browns and moss greens, nectar amber, oil-sheen rainbows on the seeps”
§9: “warm steam-lamp gold and green-filtered sun in the crown”
§9: “basalt black, obsidian gloss, seam-red, ash grey, fireweed's defiant green in the flash-zones, beldon amber”
the_forge.note: Seam-red is ground/light, not flora; fireweed green sampled near #9dfb00 in existing art, tempered.

the_greentide.accentLabel: none — zero accents claimed (§8.4 allows zero)
derivedFrom: §9: “every green at once, white steam, black mud, the river's gradient from glass-clear … to milk and salt-crust”
the_greentide.note: Accent NONE drafted: “every green at once” is the spectacle; leaving the accent slot open for a future fruit/bloom commission.

the_grey_deep.accentLabel: the one impossible saturated color [INVENTED hue]
derivedFrom: §9: “every grey, bone-pale pillar mineral, crystal white on the statuary, the murk's green cast”
§9: “and one impossible saturated color, moving, rare” (prose demands the accent but names no hue)
INVENTED: accent hue — prose requires an impossible saturated color and deliberately leaves it unnamed; magenta drafted as maximally non-oceanic

derivedFrom: §9: “blue-on-black, fungal grey and green, the metal and ceramic of superb dead technology, the orange of the imported crystal”

the_miasma.accentLabel: rainbow-bloom (representative hex of a multi-hue suite)
derivedFrom: §9: “muck-browns and mangal greens, salt-crust white on the sea side”
§9: “the rainbow flora burning through it: genuine, saturated, beautiful color that means exactly what it seems to mean”
the_miasma.note: The accent species is the rainbow suite itself (3–4 blooms); one hex stands for it on this board only.

derivedFrom: §9: “black mirror, aurora green/violet, crystal-clear and frost-white, the blue of running flame”
§9: “grass-gold, ash-black in migrating bands, regrowth's shocking week-old green, fulgurite white in the black”
§9: “bone white, lilac, milk white, glow-blue and lantern-gold against wet black soil”
the_rot.note: Lantern-gold is the rival accent; glow-blue drafted because the fungal art already carries it. Owner's call.

derivedFrom: §9: “rust film over dark metal, verdigris at the coolant, the dust's ochre drifts, hazard-sulfur at the pools — and no green anywhere”
banned: green vegetation of any kind (“no green anywhere” — verdigris is mineral, not plant)

derivedFrom: §9: “boiling white, scald cyan, thermophile rainbow, basalt rim black, the peaks' cloud-cap”
§9: “rainbow mat-bands where the shallows clear”
the_scald.note: Hot-spring mat bands run yellow→orange→rust by temperature; one hex stands for the band system.

the_scarlands.accentLabel: acid-green pool (the rainbow pools' lead hue)
derivedFrom: §9: “crater-black glower crusts, rust and bone of the works, slag grey”
§9: “the rainbow pools as the only saturation on the map: acid greens, copper blues, sulfur yellows, all lying about what they are”
§9: “translucent greens and ambers, membrane pinks in the rich ground, the grey of drowned ruins”
the_slime.note: Family midpoints sampled straight off the existing slimy-flora art (#71773f–#828b5f).

derivedFrom: §9: “every black (wet, glassy, matte), horizon amber, lamp gold, the waxy grey-greens of the edge-flora, rust of the derricks”
§9: “deep greens and kelp bronze, mat-pale ceiling, mud browns in the dry-looking rivers, silver shoal-flash, lamp gold”
§9: “every dark green, dead white silk, bone-white blooms, the red-brown of hide-woven nests”
§9: “the pale flowers glowing in the dark like route-lights”
the_webwork.note: The accent is a VALUE spike (near-white), not a hue — deliberate: silk and blooms own brightness here.

derivedFrom: §9: “salt white, ash grey, vitrified black-green, brine-pool mineral color — and the sickly radiances against it”
wasteland.note: Existing toxi-flora art samples violet (#6f267c, #4e2f56) — the “sickly radiance” drafted violet to match it rather than glow-green.

derivedFrom: §9: “bone-white sunlit stone; wet black weep-streaks; green held in blue shade; verdigris where metal meets moss”

wreck_fields.accentLabel: verdigris (one saturated hue per patch — rotating)
derivedFrom: §9: “cold grey-blue ground and sky · bright bare metal — silver, gunmetal”
§9: “one saturated hue per patch, and never the same hue twice in a shot: verdigris here, titanium white there, a bad yellow-green”
banned: rust orange (“No rust orange anywhere” — hard sheet ban)
wreck_fields.note: The accent ROTATES per patch by sheet law; verdigris drafted as the board's stand-in.
